iPhone Ultra launch event is just weeks away, but a new report suggests initial supply may be extremely limited, with early availability potentially restricted to the U.S. market only.

iPhone Ultra supply tight; early launch may be limited to U.S. market

Apple will hold an event in the U.S. on September 8, at which it will unveil its first foldable iPhone — though the product will not go on sale immediately. A major Chinese component supplier has confirmed that Apple is facing challenges in supply, testing and pricing, which could mean the Australian market will have to wait several months to see the device. The supplier told ChannelNews that the delay is "mainly due to supply and pricing issues," adding: "We believe Apple is also encountering difficulties in prototype testing." Australian telecoms carriers and a major retailer have both confirmed that this "Apple Fold" will not appear on local retail shelves this time. Due to limited supply, the product will launch first in the U.S. before expanding to other major markets such as China.

Previous rumours have suggested iPhone Ultra supply could be very tight at launch. If true, making the U.S. the short-term initial launch market would also be a reasonable move.

Although this report sounds quite plausible, there is still reason to remain sceptical.

Firstly, the report mentions the event will be held on September 8, but Apple will almost certainly not choose that date.

Holding the event on the second Tuesday of September has always been a safe choice, but this year the U.S. Labor Day falls slightly later, on September 7. It would be extremely unwise for Apple to hold an iPhone launch event the day after Labor Day. Wednesday, September 9 is actually more likely.

Furthermore, the sources for this report appear to come from China and Australia. If the iPhone Ultra is not launching in those regions in the short term, it is reasonable for local insiders to learn about it in advance. But they may not know whether the device will be sold exclusively in the U.S. at launch — that claim looks more like speculation.

Regardless, it would not be surprising for Apple to roll out the iPhone Ultra gradually. Being able to ship in the U.S. in September and then gradually expand to more markets is better than postponing the entire launch event.

When do you expect to get your hands on an iPhone Ultra? Let us know in the comments.
